findings.title: add_members reads params[:group_id] but route only exposes :id
findings.body: The new add_members action does `Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)`, but the route in config/routes.rb defines `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` as a member route inside `resources :groups`, which only populates `params[:id]`, not `params[:group_id]`. The client in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js sends `PUT /admin/groups/${group.id}/members.json`, so `params[:group_id]` will be nil and `params.require(:group_id)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` in production. The action should read `params[:id]` (or the route should be expressed so that the ID arrives as `group_id`).

findings.title: remove_member reads params[:group_id] but route only exposes :id
findings.body: Same root cause as the add_members finding above: `remove_member` reads `params.require(:group_id)`, while the DELETE member route only sets `params[:id]`. The JS sends `DELETE /admin/groups/${group.id}/members.json?user_id=...`, so `params[:group_id]` is nil and the action will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` in production, breaking member removal.

findings.title: totalPages off-by-one for exact multiples, exposing an empty last page
findings.body: `totalPages` returns `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For user_count=50, limit=50 it returns 2 instead of 1; for user_count=100, limit=50 it returns 3 instead of 2. The `next` action uses `showingLast = propertyEqual(currentPage, totalPages)` to decide when to stop, so with the inflated totalPages the user can click Next past the last real page and `findMembers` will be invoked with `offset == user_count`, returning an empty result page that is still displayed. Should use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (or `Math.floor((user_count - 1) / limit) + 1`).

findings.title: remove_member test uses wrong HTTP verb (PUT vs DELETE)
findings.body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the route is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. RSpec controller specs invoke actions directly and largely ignore the verb, so this test happens to pass via the automatic-group short-circuit, but it does not exercise the real DELETE route and would not catch the param-name mismatch above. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...` (and ideally drive the test through routing).

findings.title: Tests pass group_id directly, bypassing routing and hiding the route bug
findings.body: Every new test passes `group_id: <id>` (or `:user_id`) directly as a hash parameter, so RSpec never goes through the route table and `params[:group_id]` is supplied even though the route only sets `params[:id]`. That is why the `params.require(:group_id)` bug appears to work in the controller spec but will fail in production. Switch to `id:` and/or add a request/integration spec that hits the real URL.

findings.title: group.users.delete(user_id) replaces the safer group.remove(user) pattern
findings.body: The previous implementation used `group.remove(user)` to drop just the membership. The new code calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` with a raw integer. Behaviour depends on the association: for `has_many` without `through` Rails may resolve the id and destroy the User record; for `has_many :through`/`HABTM` only the join row is removed, but the internal lookup raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` if the id does not exist — losing the previous silent no-op for unknown users and risking a 500. Prefer `group.users.find_by(id: user_id)&.delete` (or rescue membership), and keep the pattern consistent with `add_members` which still uses `group.add(user)`.

findings.title: add_members silently drops stripped or unknown usernames
findings.body: `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` neither strips whitespace nor skips blanks, so a value like `"alice, bob,carol"` (space after the first comma) tries `User.find_by_username(" bob")` and silently fails to add that user. Additionally, unknown usernames are silently ignored with no error in the response, so the admin gets a 200 success even when none of the supplied names were applied. At minimum strip each entry and skip blanks, and consider returning the list of unrecognised names so the UI can warn.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined when group has no name
findings.body: `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }` returns `undefined` rather than a resolved promise. The two current callers (admin_group_route and group-members route) ignore the return value, but any future caller chaining `.then(...)` would throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'then' of undefined`. Return `Ember.RSVP.resolve()` for consistency with the previous version that returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`.

findings.title: Group#addMembers / #removeMember have no error handler
findings.body: The `Discourse.ajax` call in `addMembers` (and `removeMember`) registers only a `.then` success handler that triggers `self.findMembers()`. There is no rejection handler, so a 4xx/5xx response (group validation failure, network error, or the route bug above) is swallowed and the admin sees no feedback that the operation actually failed. Add a second argument to `.then` (or `.catch`) that surfaces a `bootbox.alert` like the save action does.
